priorities.finding: Request-context features are the only screened group with positive overall primary lift (+0.00221), full coverage, and positive lift on all four temporal holdout days. The gain is modest and variable, so retain and prioritize this group rather than expecting a large standalone improvement.
priorities.recommended_action: Keep tab, hour, and weekday in the next budgeted model; validate their incremental effect with a fresh temporal holdout before adding complexity.

avoid: Do not spend further budget on user_profile, historical_user_author_affinity, upload_recency, content_duration, item_metadata, historical_author_response, or historical_item_response; all have non-positive screening lift, with the historical response groups showing especially large and consistent losses. Cite: screen:user_profile, screen:historical_user_author_affinity, screen:upload_recency, screen:content_duration, screen:item_metadata, screen:historical_author_response, screen:historical_item_response.

Do not use forbidden current-impression outcomes or quarantined aggregate snapshots because they are unavailable at ranking time or lack per-impression availability timestamps. Cite: feature:author_id, feature:item_metadata.
metric_diagnosis: Apply the strict early-stop rule to the current BPR direction: the official result reaches GAUC 0.6664 and primary 0.6008, but top-five quality remains the main weakness relative to ranking quality, with nDCG@5 0.5352 and Precision@5 0.3749. Large warm-item and warm-user segments are close to global performance, while rare items and several tabs are materially weaker; tab 8 is the clearest actionable failure with GAUC 0.4259 and nDCG@5 0.0270, whereas the zero-positive user segment has GAUC 0.5 and zero top-five metrics but is not meaningful ranking evidence because it contains no positives. Stop additional BPR budget unless a targeted intervention improves these within-user top-five weaknesses on a new temporal holdout. Cite: experiment:2:metrics, experiment:2:segment:item_frequency:rare_1_4, experiment:2:segment:tab:8, experiment:2:segment:user_positive_count:zero.
